entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Bench: Raj Beer Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
Court No. - 88
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 2488 of 2022
Revisionist :- Prashant Yadav And 2 Others

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Revisionist :-
Rakesh Chandra Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sanjay Kr. Srivastava Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the revisionists, learned counsel for the informant/opposite party No. 2 and learned A.G.A for the State.

2. The present criminal revision has been preferred against the order dated 06.04.2022, passed by the Additional District & Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Court No. 2, Meerut in session case no. 499 of 2021, arising out of case crime no. 478 of 2019, under Sections 498A, 323, 313, 504 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, police station Kankar Khera, district Meerut, whereby the application filed by the accused-revisionists under Section 227 Cr.P.C. for discharge has been rejected.

entities.text: Additional District & Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Court No. 2, Meerut
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the revisionists has submitted that the impugned order is against facts and law and thus, liable to be set aside.
The revisionist no. 1 is husband and revisionist nos. 2 and 3 are father-in-law and mother-in-law of informant.
The first information report was lodged by the informant making false and baseless allegations.

The marriage of informant with revisionist no. 1 took place on 21.02.2019 and thereafter she has gone to her parental home on 05.03.2019 and after Prashant Yadav And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97075972/
1 that she has never met with her husband.

entities.text: Prashant Yadav And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The allegation that on 29.03.2019 her husband has given some medicines to her and resultantly she has suffered miscarriage, is thoroughly false and that no case under Section 313 IPC is made out.

Referring to the facts of the matter, it was submitted that no prima facie case is made out against the revisionists and thus, the court below has committed error by rejecting application of revisionists for discharge.

4. Per contra, learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the informant/opposite party No. 2 have opposed the revision and argued that in the first information report, there are clear allegations that all the accused-revisionists used to demand Rs. 10 lacs in additional dowry from the informant and she was harassed on that account.
It was submitted that on 29.03.2019 revisionist no. 1 has given some medicines to her and resultantly she has suffered miscarriage.
Referring to the facts of the matter and material collected during investigation, it was submitted that a prima facie case is made out against the revisionists.

It was further submitted that the trial court has considered all relevant facts and material while rejecting the application of revisionists for discharge and there is no illegality or perversity in the impugned order.
5. I have considered rival submissions and perused record.
6. It is well settled that at the stage of framing of charge or considering discharge application, the court is not to analyse reliability of the material on record.
The evidentiary value and its credibility has to be considered at the stage of trial.
Marshalling and appreciation of evidence is not in the domain of the court at that point of time.

At the stage of consideration of an application for discharge, the court has to proceed with an assumption that the material brought on record by prosecution is true and such material and documents have to be considered with a view to find out whether the facts emerging from such material when taken at their face value disclose the existence of all the ingredients constituting the offence.

7. In State of Bihar v. Ramesh Singh [ (1977) 4 SCC 39], considering the scope of Sections 227 and 228 of the Code, it was held that at the stage of framing of charge it is not obligatory for the Judge to consider in any detail and weigh in a sensitive balance whether the facts, if proved, would be incompatible with the innocence of the accused or not.

entities.text: State of Bihar v. Ramesh Singh [ (1977) 4 SCC 39]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At that stage, the court is not to see whether there is sufficient ground for conviction of the accused or whether the trial is sure to end in his conviction.

Strong suspicion, at the initial stage of framing of charge, is sufficient to frame the charge and in that event it is not open to say that there is no sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

8. In Superintendent and Remembrancer of legal Affairs, West Bengal v. Anil Kumar Bhunja & Ors [(1980) 1 SCR 323], the Apex Court held that the Magistrate at the stage of framing charges had to see whether the facts alleged and sought to be proved by the prosecution prima facie disclose the commission of offence on general consideration of the materials placed before him by the investigating police officer.

entities.text: Superintendent and Remembrancer of legal Affairs, West Bengal v. Anil Kumar Bhunja & Ors [(1980) 1 SCR 323]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. In State of Delhi v. Gyan Devi and Others [(2000) 8 SCC 239], the Hon'ble Supreme Court reiterated that at the stage of framing of charge the trial court is not to examine and assess in detail Prashant Yadav And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97075972/
2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the materials placed on record by the prosecution nor is it for the court to consider the sufficiency of the materials to establish the offence alleged against the accused persons.

10. In State of Maharashtra v. Priya Sharan Maharaj and Others [(1997) 4 SCC 393] it was held that at Sections 227 and 228 Cr.P.C. stage the court is required to evaluate the material and documents on record with a view to finding out if the facts emerging therefrom taken at their face value disclose the existence of all the ingredients constituting the alleged offence.

entities.text: State of Maharashtra v. Priya Sharan Maharaj and Others [(1997) 4 SCC 393]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The court may, for this limited purpose, sift the evidence as it cannot be expected even at that initial stage to accept all that the prosecution states as gospel truth even if it is opposed to common sense or the broad probabilities of the case.
11. It is apparent from the above discussed decisions of Hon'ble Apex Court that at the stage of charge there can only be limited evaluation of materials and documents on record.

At the stage of charge or consideration of an application for discharge, the court has to proceed with an assumption that the material brought on record by prosecution is true and such material and documents have to be considered with a view to find out whether the facts emerging from such material when taken at their face value disclose the existence of all the ingredients constituting the offence.

12. In the instant matter, perusal of record shows that revisionists are named in the first information report, wherein there are clear allegations that all the accused-revisionists used to demand Rs. 10 lacs in additional dowry from the informant and she was harassed on that account.
On 29.03.2019 revisionist no. 1 has given some medicines to her and resultantly she has suffered miscarriage.
In view of the allegations made in the first information report and the material collected during investigation, it cannot be said that no prima facie case is made out against the revisionists.
The court below has considered all relevant facts and material on record while rejecting the application of revisionists for discharge.
There is no illegality, perversity or error of jurisdiction in the impugned order.
The revision lacks merit and thus, liable to be dismissed.
13. With the aforesaid observations, the instant criminal revision is dismissed.
